title: Periconceptional folic acid/multivitamin supplementation and twin pregnancy
journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
population: Control mothers of the Hungarian Case-Control Surveillance of Congenital Abnormalities, 1980-1996, by pre- and postconceptional use of folic acid (in general 6 mg), multivitamins with 0.1 to 1.0 mg folic acid, or both
funder: not stated in the abstract; full text not accessible
result: Results read from the published abstract. 395 of 38,151 women had twins. Twin births 0.78% without supplements and 1.52% after preconceptional supplementation (adjusted OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.14 to 2.85); 1.14%, 1.45% and 2.00% after postconceptional folic acid, multivitamin, and both. The authors describe their earlier randomised trial as suggesting more twin pregnancies with a folic acid-containing multivitamin.
